about: Explanations for the Conjugation tab. Conjugated words are NEVER written here: each example names a lemma and a form, and js/conjugate.js produces the text, so tables and examples cannot disagree. Lemma classes are cross-checked by tests against the JMdict-verified curriculum items. Example sentences are constructed for this app and reviewed against the cited grammar reference; they are labelled as constructed in the UI.

jmdict.name: JMdict/EDRDG part-of-speech tags (verb and adjective classes of every curriculum item)

groups.name: Group 1 verbs
groups.summary: The final kana changes along its row of the kana chart (書か・書き・書く・書け・書こ). Every verb not ending in る is Group 1 — and so are many verbs that DO end in る.
groups.how: Find the ending kana. Negative: move to the あ-row + ない (う becomes わ: 買わない). Polite: い-row + ます. Potential / ば / imperative: え-row. Volitional: お-row + う. The て/た forms follow the sound changes below.

te_rules.note: except 行く → 行って / 行った

patterns.note: Looks like Group 2 but is Group 1. You cannot tell from the dictionary form alone — the dictionary class decides.
死ぬ is the only common verb ending in ぬ; it is shown here only to complete the pattern.

exceptions.note: て/た forms are 行って / 行った (not 行いて).
Plain negative is simply ない (never あらない); past negative なかった.

groups.name: Group 2 verbs
groups.summary: Always end in る, preceded by an い- or え-sound (食べる, 見る). Drop る and add the ending — nothing else changes.
groups.how: Stem = remove る (食べ). Polite: stem + ます. Negative: stem + ない. て-form: stem + て. Potential and passive: stem + られる. Causative: stem + させる. Volitional: stem + よう. Imperative: stem + ろ.
groups.warning: Not every 〜いる/〜える verb is Group 2: 帰る, 入る, 知る, 走る are Group 1. Check the class shown on each word card.

groups.name: Irregular verbs
groups.summary: Only two: する (to do) and 来る (to come). する also forms thousands of compound verbs (勉強する, 予約する) that conjugate exactly like する.
groups.how: Memorise them. 来る keeps its kanji but changes reading: 来ない (こない), 来ます (きます), 来る (くる), 来れば (くれば), 来い (こい).

groups.name: い-adjectives
groups.summary: End in い and conjugate themselves: drop the final い and add くない, かった, くて, ければ…
groups.how: Stem = remove い (高). Negative 高くない · past 高かった · past negative 高くなかった · て-form 高くて · adverb 高く. Polite: add です (高いです, 高くないです / 高くありません).

patterns.note: いい conjugates from よい: よくない, よかった, よくて — never いくない.

exceptions.note: All forms except いい / いいです are built on よ-: よくない, よかった.

groups.name: な-adjectives
groups.summary: Behave like nouns: they take だ/です and need な before a noun (静かな部屋).
groups.how: Plain 静かだ · polite 静かです · negative 静かじゃない (formal: ではない) · past 静かだった · before a noun 静かな · adverb 静かに · て-form 静かで.

patterns.note: End in い but are な-adjectives: きれいじゃない, not きれくない.

exceptions.note: 好き and 嫌い take が for the thing liked: 抹茶が好きです.

forms.name: Dictionary form (plain present)
forms.label: 辞書形
forms.means: Plain, non-past: "do / will do". The form listed in dictionaries.
forms.use: Casual speech with friends and family; inside longer sentences (before nouns, before と/なら/な, etc.) even in polite speech.

build.irregular: する / 来る

mistakes: Using it to a shop clerk or stranger sounds abrupt — use the ます form.

forms.name: Polite present
forms.label: ます形
forms.use: Default with anyone you don't know well: shops, restaurants, staff, neighbours, colleagues.

build.irregular: します / 来ます (きます)

mistakes: Group 1 る-verbs: 帰ります, not 帰ます.

forms.name: Polite negative
forms.label: ません
forms.use: Declining politely, stating what you don't do.

build.group1: い-row + ません (書きません)
build.irregular: しません / 来ません

forms.name: Polite past
forms.label: ました
forms.use: Talking about what happened, politely.

build.irregular: しました / 来ました

forms.name: Polite past negative
forms.label: ませんでした
forms.use: Saying something did not happen, politely.

build.irregular: しませんでした / 来ませんでした

forms.name: Plain negative
forms.label: ない形
forms.means: Casual "don't / won't". Also the base for many patterns (ないでください, なければ).
forms.use: Casual speech; inside sentences.

build.group1: あ-row + ない; う → わ (買わない); ある → ない
build.irregular: しない / 来ない (こない)

mistakes: 買う → 買わない (not 買あない).
ある → ない (not あらない).

forms.name: Plain past (た-form)
forms.label: た形
forms.means: Casual "did". Same sound changes as the て-form, with た/だ.
forms.use: Casual speech; before nouns (昨日見た映画 = the film I saw yesterday); in patterns (たことがある, たら).

build.group1: like て-form with た/だ (書いた, 読んだ, 買った)
build.irregular: した / 来た (きた)

mistakes: 行く → 行った (not 行いた).

forms.name: Plain past negative
forms.label: なかった
forms.use: Casual speech; inside sentences.

build.group1: あ-row + なかった (ある → なかった)
build.irregular: しなかった / 来なかった (こなかった)

forms.name: て-form
forms.label: て形
forms.means: Joins actions in sequence ("…and then…") and is the base for requests, permission, ongoing actions and more.
forms.use: Linking actions; giving directions; building ください / ている / てもいい.

build.group1: う・つ・る→って · む・ぶ・ぬ→んで · く→いて · ぐ→いで · す→して (行く→行って)
build.irregular: して / 来て (きて)

mistakes: Mixing up the sound changes: 読んで (not 読って), 書いて (not 書って).

examples.jp: 次の駅で{v}、バスに乗ります。
examples.en: I get off at the next station and take a bus.

forms.name: 〜ている (ongoing / resulting state)
forms.label: ている
forms.means: Either an action in progress ("am eating") or a state that results from a change ("know", "live in", "am married").
forms.use: For verbs of action it means "-ing". For change-of-state verbs (知る, 住む, 結婚する) it describes the current state. In speech often shortened to 〜てる.

build.irregular: している / 来ている

mistakes: "I know" is 知っています, not 知ります.
"I live in Kyoto" is 京都に住んでいます.

forms.name: Potential (can do)
forms.label: 可能形
forms.means: "Can / be able to". The result is a Group 2 verb (話せる → 話せます).
forms.use: Abilities and possibilities. The object often takes が instead of を: 日本語が話せます.

build.group1: え-row + る (書ける, 話せる)
build.group2: stem + られる (食べられる); casual speech often drops ら: 食べれる
build.irregular: する → できる · 来る → 来られる (こられる)

mistakes: する has no potential of its own: use できる (勉強できる).
Some verbs have no natural potential, e.g. 分かる already means "can understand".

examples.en: I can speak a little Japanese.

forms.name: Passive
forms.label: 受身形
forms.means: "Be done (by someone)". The doer is marked with に. Also used when something unwelcome happens to you, and as a light honorific.
forms.use: News, notices, complaints ("my bike was taken"), and polite references to a superior's actions.

build.group1: あ-row + れる (書かれる; う→わ: 買われる)
build.group2: stem + られる (same shape as the potential!)
build.irregular: される / 来られる

mistakes: For Group 2 verbs the passive and potential look identical (食べられる) — context decides.

examples.en: I was called by name by the teacher.

forms.name: Causative (make / let)
forms.label: 使役形
forms.means: "Make or let someone do". The everyday win: 〜させてください = "please let me…".
forms.use: Asking permission politely: 少し休ませてください (let me rest a little), 考えさせてください (let me think about it).

build.group1: あ-row + せる (書かせる; う→わ: 買わせる)
build.irregular: させる / 来させる (こさせる)

examples.en: Please let me rest a little.

forms.name: Volitional (let's / I'll)
forms.label: 意向形
forms.use: Casual invitations among friends; with と思う for plans (行こうと思う = I'm thinking of going).

build.group1: お-row + う (行こう, 帰ろう)
build.irregular: しよう / 来よう (こよう)

forms.name: Polite "let's / shall we"
forms.label: ましょう
forms.means: Polite "let's…"; with か, "shall we / shall I…?"
forms.use: Suggesting a plan; offering help (持ちましょうか = shall I carry it?). To INVITE someone politely, 〜ませんか (won't you…?) is gentler.

build.irregular: しましょう / 来ましょう

mistakes: Inviting someone with ましょうか can sound like it's already decided; 一緒に行きませんか leaves them room to decline.

forms.name: Want to (〜たい)
forms.label: たい
forms.means: "I want to…". Conjugates like an い-adjective (行きたくない, 行きたかった).
forms.use: Your own wishes; asking a friend what they want. For other people's wishes use 〜たがっている. Asking a superior 〜たいですか directly can sound blunt.
forms.register: neutral (add です to be polite)

build.irregular: したい / 来たい

mistakes: The object can take が or を: 抹茶が飲みたい / 抹茶を飲みたい — both are fine.

forms.name: Please do (〜てください)
forms.label: てください
forms.use: Everyday requests to staff, strangers, colleagues. Softer still: 〜てもらえますか / 〜ていただけますか (could you…?).

build.irregular: してください / 来てください

mistakes: Polite in form, but still a request — to a superior, a question (〜ていただけますか) is gentler.

forms.name: Please don't (〜ないでください)
forms.label: ないでください
forms.use: Asking someone not to do something; common on notices.

build.irregular: しないでください / 来ないでください

forms.name: Imperative (command)
forms.label: 命令形
forms.use: You will SEE and HEAR it (road signs such as 止まれ, emergencies, sports, rough casual speech) far more than you should say it. Saying it to people is rude or aggressive.
forms.warning: Do not use when asking people for things — use 〜てください.

build.irregular: しろ / 来い (こい)

examples.en: Get over here, quick! (blunt — recognise, don't use)

forms.name: Prohibition (〜な)
forms.label: 禁止形
forms.use: Warning signs and emergencies (入るな = Keep out). Not for normal conversation.
forms.warning: Recognise it on signs; to ask people not to do something use 〜ないでください.

build.irregular: するな / 来るな

mistakes: Don't confuse it with the soft sentence-ending な ("…isn't it") — the prohibitive attaches to the bare dictionary form, usually said sharply.

forms.name: Conditional 〜ば
forms.label: ば形
forms.means: "If A (then B)" — focuses on the condition that has to be met.
forms.use: Asking for advice: どうすればいいですか (what should I do?). General if-statements. Less natural than たら before a request or your own intention when A is an action.

build.irregular: すれば / 来れば (くれば)

forms.name: Conditional 〜たら
forms.label: たら
forms.means: "If / when A happens, B" — A is completed first. The most versatile conditional in conversation.
forms.use: Plans and requests that follow an event: 着いたら電話してください. Also "when I did A, I found B".

build.irregular: したら / 来たら

examples.en: I'll call when I get home.

forms.name: Conditional 〜と
forms.label: と
forms.means: "Whenever / if A, B (naturally follows)" — automatic, habitual or inevitable results.
forms.use: Directions (go straight and you'll see…), how machines work, habits. B cannot be a request, invitation or your intention.

build.irregular: すると / 来ると

mistakes: ✗ 駅に着くと電話してください — a request needs たら: 駅に着いたら電話してください.

examples.jp: まっすぐ{v}、右に駅があります。
examples.en: Go straight and the station is on your right.

forms.name: Conditional 〜なら
forms.label: なら
forms.means: "If (it's the case that) A / if you're going to A" — responds to a situation or to what someone just said.
forms.use: Recommendations based on someone's plan: 京都に行くなら… B can even happen before A.

build.irregular: するなら / 来るなら

examples.jp: 嵐山に{v}、朝早いほうがいいですよ。
examples.en: If you're going to Arashiyama, it's better to go early in the morning.

forms.name: Permission 〜てもいい
forms.label: てもいい
forms.means: "It's OK to…"; as a question, "May I…?"
forms.use: Asking permission: これを使ってもいいですか.

build.irregular: してもいい / 来てもいい

forms.name: Must not 〜てはいけない
forms.label: てはいけない
forms.use: Rules. Strong; casual speech uses 〜ちゃだめ / 〜じゃだめ.

build.irregular: してはいけません / 来てはいけません

examples.jp: 電車の中で大きな声で{v}。
examples.en: You must not talk loudly on the train.

forms.name: Must / have to
forms.label: なければならない
forms.means: "Have to…" (literally "if I don't, it won't do").
forms.use: Obligations. Casual: 〜なきゃ / 〜ないと. いけません and なりません are interchangeable here.

build.group1: あ-row + なければなりません
build.group2: stem + なければなりません
build.irregular: しなければ / 来なければ

examples.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.

forms.name: Don't have to
forms.label: なくてもいい
forms.use: Relieving someone of an obligation.

build.irregular: しなくてもいい / 来なくてもいい

examples.en: You don't have to come tomorrow.

forms.name: Experience 〜たことがある
forms.label: たことがある
forms.use: Conversation starters: 〜たことがありますか (have you ever…?).

build.irregular: したことがある / 来たことがある

mistakes: Not for things done regularly or very recently.

examples.en: Have you ever seen a Japanese film?

forms.name: Plain present
forms.label: 普通形
forms.means: "Is …" (casual). な-adjectives add だ, which is often dropped in casual speech.
forms.use: Casual speech; い-adjectives also go directly before nouns.
mistakes: Don't put だ after an い-adjective: ✗ 高いだ.

forms.name: Polite present
forms.label: です
forms.use: Default with people you don't know well.

examples.en: This ramen is delicious, isn't it?

forms.name: Negative
forms.label: 否定
forms.use: Often with あまり: あまり暑くない (not very hot).

build.i: drop い + くない (高くない; いい → よくない)
build.na: + じゃない (formal: ではない)

mistakes: いい → よくない, not いくない.
きれい is a な-adjective: きれいじゃない, not きれくない.

forms.name: Polite negative
forms.label: 否定（丁寧）
forms.use: くないです / じゃないです is conversational; くありません / ではありません is a little more formal.

build.i: くないです or くありません
build.na: じゃないです / ではありません

forms.name: Past
forms.label: 過去

build.i: drop い + かった (高かった; いい → よかった)

mistakes: ✗ 暑いでした — say 暑かったです.

forms.name: Polite past
forms.label: 過去（丁寧）

build.i: かったです (高かったです)

mistakes: い-adjectives never take でした: ✗ 美味しいでした.

forms.name: Past negative
forms.label: 過去否定
forms.means: "Was not …" (casual; add です to be polite).

build.i: くなかった (よくなかった)

forms.name: て-form (and…)
forms.label: て形
forms.use: Describing something with two qualities.

build.i: drop い + くて (大きくて)

forms.name: Before a noun
forms.label: 連体形
forms.use: い-adjectives go straight before the noun; な-adjectives need な.
mistakes: ✗ 静か部屋 / ✗ 高いな店.

examples.en: I went to a famous temple.

forms.name: Adverb
forms.label: 連用形
forms.means: Describing how an action is done.

build.i: drop い + ければ (よければ)

examples.jp: 天気が{v}、散歩しましょう。
examples.en: If the weather is nice, let's go for a walk.

build.na: だったら (静かだったら)

examples.jp: {v}、エアコンをつけてください。
examples.en: If it's hot, please turn on the air conditioner.

forms.name: Become (〜くなる / 〜になる)
forms.label: なる
forms.use: Changes: 暑くなりましたね (it's got hot, hasn't it).

build.na: に + なる (便利になる)

forms.name: Too … (〜すぎる)
forms.label: すぎる
forms.use: Complaining or declining: 高すぎます (it's too expensive).

build.i: drop い + すぎる (高すぎる)
